texts.preamble: Kedar Nath vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ... on 23 July, 2021 Author: Saroj Yadav Bench: Saroj Yadav High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench ?Court No. - 31 Case :- U/S 482/378/407 No. - 2327 of 2021 Applicant :- Kedar Nath Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. & Ors. Counsel for Applicant :- Vijay Bahadur Yadav,Jay Prakas Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A. Hon'ble Mrs. Saroj Yadav,J. This petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed to quash the notice dated 02.03.2020 under Section 111 Cr.P.C. issued by opposite party no. 2 and order dated 10.12.2020 passed by Sessions Judge, Sultanpur.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that there is only one case against the petitioner under Sections 323, 325, 354, 504, 506 IPC. In that case the petitioner has been enlarged on bail but the opposite party no. 2-Sub Divisional Magistrate, Tehsil Kadipur, District Sultanpur without any basis has issued notice under Section 111 Cr.P.C asking the applicant to show cause why he may not be required to furnish a personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/- and two sureties in the like amount for Kedar Nath vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ... on 23 July, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71543254/ 1 maintaining peace and good conduct for a period of three years. He further submitted that the petitioner is a Teacher and he has falsely been implicated in the crime. He is not a habitual offender to be covered under Section 110 Cr.P.C. On being asked, learned A.G.A could not satisfy the Court regarding the issuance of notice under Section 111 Cr.P.C. against the petitioner, on the basis of Challan report dated 27.02.2020 of Officer in-charge, Kotwali Kadipur, District Sultanpur, describing the petitioner as hazardous and dangerous to the society. Section 110 of Cr.P.C. runs as under:- "110. Security for good behaviour from habitual offenders.- When (an Executive Magistrate) receives information that there is within his local jurisdiction a person who- (a) is by habit a robber, house-breaker, thief, or forger, or (b) is by habit a receiver of stolen property knowing the same to have been stolen, or (c) habitually protects or harbours thieves, or aids in the concealment or disposal of stolen property, or (d) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of, the offence of kidnapping, abduction, extortion, cheating or mischief, or any offence punishable under Chapter II of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860), or under Section 489-A, Section 489-B, Section 489-C or Section 489-D of that Code, or (e) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of, offences, involving a breach of the peace, or (f) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of- (i)any offence under one or more of the following Act, namely :- (a) the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 (23 of 1940); (b) the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973 (46 of 1973) ; ( c) the Employees' Provident Fund (and Family Pension Fund) Act, 1952 (19 of 1952) (d) the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (37 of 1954) ; (e) the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955) ; Kedar Nath vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ... on 23 July, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71543254/ 2 (f) the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 (22 of 1955); (g) the Customs Act, 1962 (52 of 1962) ; (h) the Foreigners Act, 1946 (3 of 1946) ; or (ii) any offence punishable under any other law providing for the prevention of hoarding or profiteering or of adulteration of food or drugs or of corruption, or (g) is so desperate and dangerous as to render his being at large without security hazardous to the community, Such Magistrate may, in the manner hereinafter provided, require such person to show cause why he should not be ordered to execute a bond, with sureties, for his good behaviour for such period, not exceeding three years, as the Magistrate thinks fit. It is essential that before seeking personal bond from any person, satisfaction is to be recorded by the Magistrate in order to ensure that the person comes within the ambit of Section 110(a) to (g).
